gen-eater-gf-khula: Dark and snarling: Eater's thin strokes stay surprisingly sturdy. Khula settles below with a tall midsection and curves that hold their mouths open, so a long block of text slides by easily.
gen-eater-gf-krub: Eater's thin strokes keep a surprising sturdiness beside slightly heavier stems, with wide gaps between the letters. But Krub, with its pronounced x-height and open-ended curves, makes a long run of text feel easy going.
gen-eater-gf-kufam: Smooth as neon tubing, this plain sans never shifts weight along a curve. Kufam's single track width sits under Eater's darker, gently varied strokes, which lets the heading's menace stand out.
gen-eater-gf-martel-sans: Martel Sans reads openly, with generous curves and a high mean line running across every word. And after Eater's soft contrast and dark mood, the text glides along without tiring the eye.
gen-eater-gf-michroma: Eater arrives dark and aggressive, with wide gaps between letters. Michroma then gives each sans letter a wide berth and curves full of daylight, so text moves slowly and spaciously.
gen-eater-gf-mozilla-text: Tall bodies and outward-flaring terminals make this sans-serif look bold. Mozilla Text works beneath Eater's dark, modestly contrasted letters, giving the whole layout a firmer footing than the heading alone.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-buhid: Menacing letters up top, tidy ones below. Eater does dark drama with sturdy thin strokes, while Noto Sans Buhid stays quiet, with generous space around its curves and a high-set x-height.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-carian: Noto Sans Carian keeps its terminals apart like scissor blades. Beside Eater's dark, aggressive heading, this plain sans feels tidy and restrained, giving the two a push-and-pull mood.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-chakma: Approachable describes Noto Sans Chakma, a plain sans whose s and c stay uncrowded. And Eater does the dark, soft-contrast drama best, leaving the body to keep things friendly.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-cherokee: Professional but friendly, this sans-serif packs a tall band of letters under short stalks. Noto Sans Cherokee handles the quiet work, while Eater brings the dark, sturdy-hairlined bite up front.
